- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is trending down, model often underestimates further decline; add 1–3% downward bias for next 7–14 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 65% of 30-day moving average of history, model tends to be too optimistic; apply 5–10% downward correction.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.6) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 7-day average of true prices as anchor for correction.
